fields.description:
## Observation

`reduce_all_tickets` (src/rebar/reducer/_api.py) applies `exclude_archived`, `exclude_deleted` and `exclude_session_logs` only after its loop finishes, and callers filter only after it returns, so every ticket that will be discarded is held in memory until then. Code reviews are 3,439 of 9,727 store directories. Measured on an isolated copy of the live store, 2026-10-29 (tracemalloc peak during the call, current caches):

| Read | Peak now | Peak with an in-loop filter and field trim | Output compared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` (`reads.py` `search_state`, full state, 141 matches) | 348.8 MB | 24.6 MB | identical (141 = 141) |
| `recent_session_logs` (full state, keeps 5) | 284.3 MB | 10.8 MB | identical |
| `bridge_fsck` binding-drift step (uses ticket_id, status, archived) | 328.6 MB | 69.5 MB (66.3 MB of it is binding/Jira data) | drift counts identical |
| `validate` (full-body list) | 284.3 MB | 49.3 MB | report identical |
| `ticket_deps` on a graph-cache miss | 284.9 MB | 64.2 MB | not compared |
| `list_tickets --status=open` | 64.1 MB | 11.0 MB | ids identical |
| `list_tickets` with `blocking_state` (holds pass 1 during `find_ready_tickets`) | 106.6 MB | not prototyped | — |

I confirmed the `search_state` and `recent_session_logs_state` calls and the post-loop filters by reading the code.

Re-measured on a fresh copy, 2026-10-29, before any change (peaks reproduce): search full 348.9 MB, recent_session_logs 284.4 MB, binding drift 328.7 MB, validate 284.4 MB, deps cache miss 284.5 MB.

Findings from reading the code that change the plan:
- The binding-drift step lives in `src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck_drift.py` (not `_commands/`). It reduces with no exclusions and reports every non-bound local ticket, including session logs and code reviews, as `unbound_local`, so it can only be trimmed (to `ticket_id`/`id`/`status`/`archived`; `reconciler/classify.local_state` reads only `archived` and `status`), not filtered.
- About 18 test modules replace `reduce_all_tickets` with stubs that ignore keyword arguments. Callers therefore keep their existing post-loop filters (they are pure predicates, so applying them a second time is a no-op on real data); the in-loop predicate only pre-narrows.
- `list_states` counts children over the reduced set before narrowing filters, so it can pre-filter in the loop only when neither `min_children` nor `with_children_count` is requested; otherwise it keeps the current path.
- Search matching happens in `search_states` (src/rebar/reducer/search.py); the in-loop matcher must be the same code, so it is split into a compiled per-ticket predicate that `search_states` also uses. Jira keys must be attached before matching because the haystack includes `jira_key`.

## Plan
1. Give `reduce_all_tickets` two optional keyword arguments: `keep` (a per-ticket predicate, applied after the existing exclusions) and `keep_fields` (a whitelist projection, the counterpart of `omit_fields`). Apply `exclude_archived`, `exclude_deleted` and `exclude_session_logs` inside the loop, so a discarded ticket is never appended. Error dicts keep their current treatment.
2. Move each caller onto it, keeping its post-loop filtering:
   - `search_state`: attach the Jira key and run the compiled search predicate inside the loop.
   - `recent_session_logs_state`: keep only session logs, project to `ticket_id`/`created_at`, sort, then re-reduce the top N in full.
   - `audit_binding_drift` (`_load_local_by_id`): project to `ticket_id`/`id`/`status`/`archived`.
   - `validate` (`_raw_tickets`): drop `closed`/`error`/`fsck_needed` inside the loop (`normalize_issues` discards them anyway), same exclusions and order as `list_states`.
   - `graph/_loader.load_indexed_states` (used by `ticket_deps` on a cache miss): drop unusable statuses in the loop and omit the body/signature fields the graph never reads (the `_READY_OMITTED_FIELDS` set).
   - `list_states`: pre-filter in the loop with the same `apply_ticket_filters` call when child counts are not requested.
3. Tests first: for each caller, a test that compares output with the old path on a fixture store containing archived, deleted, session_log and code_review tickets; a test that `reduce_all_tickets` never retains an excluded or `keep`-rejected ticket (by spying on the list it builds); and a test that each caller's projection or predicate is applied.
4. Measure each read's tracemalloc peak and compare outputs before and after on a copy of the live store, and record them on this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each read in the table returns output identical to the current code on a fixture covering archived, deleted, session_log and code_review tickets.
- [ ] Each read's peak traced memory on a clone of the live store is recorded on this ticket before and after.
- [ ] `reduce_all_tickets` retains no ticket that a caller's exclusions discard.

## File impact (expected)
- src/rebar/reducer/_api.py
- src/rebar/reducer/search.py
- src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py
- src/rebar/_engine_support/validate.py
- src/rebar/graph/_loader.py
- src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck_drift.py
- tests/unit/test_reduce_all_in_loop_filters.py
